# A sharp simplex roof bound in every dimension and direction

This is an ordinary convex-geometric theorem about one subbody of a
simplex. It is not a mixed-integer centerpoint theorem.

## 1. Statement and exact measures

Let d>=2, m=d+1, and let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole dependence
sum_i v_i=0. Let

    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for all i},        V=vol_d(T),

be the corresponding bounded full-dimensional simplex. Choose a direction
e with v_0.e=1. Use t=v_0.x as longitudinal coordinate and write
x=y+t e with y in ker(v_0). Its exact transverse measure is

    dnu(y)=dH_(d-1)(y)/||v_0||.

Let B subset T be a d-dimensional convex body of volume0<b<=V.
Write [L_B(y),U_B(y)] for its actual nonempty t sections. Fix h>d,
put H=h+1>m, and define

    R_e(B,h)=integral_(pi_e B)[h+U_B(y)]dnu(y).

Let eta in(0,1] be the unique solution of

    b/V=d eta^(d-1)-(d-1)eta^d.                       (1)

Then, for every allowed direction e,

    R_e(B,h)>=H(Vd/m)eta^(d-1).                       (2)

The bound is sharp for every b in(0,V]. If any v_i.e>0 with i!=0,
then the inequality is strict. No direction assumption is needed for
the lower bound itself.

The right side of(1) is continuous, increases strictly from0 to1
on(0,1), and has derivative d(d-1)eta^(d-2)(1-eta), so eta is
unambiguous, including its endpoint value at b=V.

## 2. Roof ratios and partial columns

Write [L(y),U(y)] for T's sections and ell=U-L. Its longitudinal
range is [-d,1]. Define the ratio

    r_e(y)=[h+U(y)]/ell(y)

on its positive-length sections. These sections fill the interior of
the transverse projection; its boundary is null. Extend B's section
length ell_B by zero off its projection. Then0<=ell_B<=ell and
integral ell_B dnu=b. Since h+L>0 and L_B>=L,

    h+U_B=ell_B+h+L_B
       >=ell_B+h+L
       >=ell_B[1+(h+L)/ell]=r_e ell_B.

Consequently, for every scalar lambda>1,

    R_e(B,h)
       >=lambda b-integral(lambda-r_e)_+ ell dnu.   (3)

Indeed pointwise r_e ell_B>=lambda ell_B-(lambda-r_e)_+ell,
using ell_B<=ell. This permits arbitrary partial columns; it does not
assume that B consists of whole T columns or minimizes any functional.

## 3. An affine overlap represents the exact dual integral

For lambda>1 define the invertible affine map

    F_lambda(y+t e)=y+[t-(t+h)/lambda]e.

It preserves y and contracts the t coordinate toward -h by factor
1-1/lambda. Because every T section lies above -h, the overlap
T intersect F_lambda(T) has section length

    [ell-(h+U)/lambda]_+.

Therefore Fubini gives the exact identity

    integral(lambda-r_e)_+ ell dnu
       =lambda vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T)).       (4)

This is one actual affine overlap; no unrelated section inclusions
have been summed.

Put

    r_i=v_i.e, p_i=(r_i)_+,
    sigma=sum_i p_i>=1,              beta=H/m>1.

Here p_0=1. We will prove

    vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T))
          <=V(1-beta/lambda)^d    for lambda>beta.   (5)

The estimate will be exact when sigma=1.

First, a direct chord inequality handles small lambda. In the standard
barycentric coordinates q_i(x)=(1-v_i.x)/m, sum q_i=1 and T is q_i>=0.
Along a chord, the positive-direction coordinates satisfy

    q_i(L)=q_i(U)+r_i ell/m       when r_i>0.

Summing them, and retaining q_0(U)=(1-U)/m, yields

    1>=sum_(r_i>0)q_i(L)>=(1-U+sigma ell)/m.

Hence sigma ell<=d+U, and thus

    r_e=(h+U)/ell
       >=sigma(h+U)/(d+U)>=sigma H/m=sigma beta.     (6)

The last ratio decreases with U because h>d, and U<=1. It is evaluated
only on positive-length chords, where d+U>0. Formula(4) consequently
vanishes if lambda<=sigma beta.

For lambda>sigma beta, the overlap is a simplex whose volume is
computable exactly. The inverse map F_lambda^(-1) adds
[(t+h)/(lambda-1)]e. For x in T this moves inward with respect to
facets having r_i<=0, since t+h>0. Only the facets with r_i>0 give
additional inequalities. Writing a=1/(lambda-1), they are

    q_i+a p_i q_0>=a p_i beta.

Introduce coordinates

    mu_i=q_i+a p_i q_0-a p_i beta.

They must all be nonnegative, with the p_i=0 coordinates unchanged.
Since p_0=1,

    q_0=(mu_0+a beta)/(1+a),
    (1-sigma/lambda)mu_0+sum_(i!=0)mu_i
                       =1-sigma beta/lambda.        (7)

Both coefficients on the right and on mu_0 are positive in this range.
Conversely every nonnegative solution of(7) reconstructs a point of
the overlap. To verify that no original T inequalities were dropped,
observe that

    mu_0<=(lambda-sigma beta)/(lambda-sigma)<1<beta.

It follows that q_0<beta, and

    q_i=mu_i+a p_i(beta-q_0)>=0

for every i. These reconstructed coordinates sum to1. The original
T inequalities and every inverse-image facet inequality therefore hold.

Use q_i, i!=0, as independent affine coordinates. Since q_0=1-sum_(i!=0)q_i,
the determinant of their map to mu_i, i!=0, is

    det[I-a(p_i)_(i!=0)(1,...,1)]
       =1-a(sigma-1)=(lambda-sigma)/(lambda-1).      (8)

The rank-one determinant identity follows directly by multilinearity
of the determinant: all terms using two columns from the rank-one
part vanish, leaving1-a sum_(i!=0)p_i. Equation(7) says that the
independent mu coordinates form the standard simplex

    mu_i>=0,          sum_(i!=0)mu_i<=1-sigma beta/lambda.

The constant Jacobian between physical volume and independent q
coordinates cancels against V. Equations(7)--(8) give exactly

    vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T))
       =V (lambda-1)/(lambda-sigma)
                              (1-sigma beta/lambda)^d. (9)

## 4. Comparison with the vertex-to-facet directions

If sigma=1, formula(9) is exactly the right side of(5). Suppose sigma>1
and lambda>sigma beta. Set

    x=(sigma-1)/(lambda-1),
    c=beta(lambda-1)/(lambda-beta).

Then0<x<1, c>1, and0<cx<1. Dividing(9) by the proposed upper bound
in(5) yields

    (1-cx)^d/(1-x)<=1,

because(1-cx)^d<=1-cx<1-x. This proves(5), strictly when sigma>1
and lambda>sigma beta. When beta<lambda<=sigma beta, the overlap
volume is0 by(6), whereas the right side of(5) is positive, so the
same strict comparison holds. Thus(5) is valid for all lambda>beta.

## 5. The exact optimization and sharp convex examples

For0<b<V choose

    lambda=beta/(1-eta)>beta,

with eta given by(1). Substituting(4)--(5) into(3),

    R_e(B,h)>=lambda[b-V(1-beta/lambda)^d]
       =lambda V[d eta^(d-1)-d eta^d]
       =H(Vd/m)eta^(d-1).

This proves(2) without presuming that an optimizer exists. When b=V,
let lambda tend to infinity in the same inequality. The finite binomial
expansion of lambda[1-(1-beta/lambda)^d] has limit d beta, yielding
R_e>=Vd beta, exactly(2) at eta=1.

For completeness, strictness when sigma>1 also holds at b=V. The exact
formula(9) and its finite expansion give

    lim_(lambda->infinity)
      lambda[V-vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T))]
        =V[d sigma beta-(sigma-1)]
        >Vd beta,

because(sigma-1)(d beta-1)>0. Applying(3)--(4) proves the strict
roof inequality at this endpoint as well. For0<b<V, strictness was
already supplied by the strict comparison in Section4 at the chosen
finite lambda.

Sharpness is realized by actual convex B when sigma=1, equivalently
r_i<=0 for every i!=0. In these directions the sole positive upper
facet is v_0.x=1, so U(y)=1 on all positive T chords. The exact simplex
chord distribution proved in
`candidate 588e75e8ff86db2e` then has maximum
length m and transverse upper-tail measure

    nu{ell>=m(1-eta)}=(Vd/m)eta^(d-1).

The chord function ell is concave on its convex transverse projection,
by interpolation of interval sections. Consequently

    B=T intersect pi_e^(-1){y:ell(y)>=m(1-eta)}

is an actual compact convex subbody. For0<eta<1 it has nonempty
interior; its volume is exactly the value in(1), by the same chord
distribution. Its upper roof is constantly1, so its cost is exactly
H(Vd/m)eta^(d-1). At eta=1 use B=T. This verifies sharpness for
every prescribed b and does not assert simultaneous equality in any
mixed-fiber criticality conditions.

An independent finite algebra audit is in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_sharp_all_dimensional_roof_overlap_defect_transport.py`.
It enumerates vertices using all original and inverse-image barycentric
inequalities in dimensions2,3,4, including below-threshold, threshold,
and positive-volume cases, and checks the optimization identity exactly.
All288 checks pass. This verification is supplementary; the arbitrary-
dimensional proof is the argument above.

## 6. Optional exact sharp capacity for a prescribed direction

The overlap formula also determines the exact minimum at every fixed
sigma, retaining the direction penalty rather than discarding it.
Keep beta=H/m>1 and sigma>=1, and define on0<=u<=1

    g(u)=u^d/sigma
           +[(sigma-1)/sigma] beta u^d/(beta-1+u).    (10)

For each b/V in(0,1] there is a unique u in(0,1] such that

    b/V=g(u)+(1-u)g'(u).                             (11)

For the fixed direction e, the exact minimum roof cost over convex
subbodies of T of volume b is

    R_min=V sigma beta g'(u).                        (12)

It depends on the direction only through sigma. This is a further
ordinary geometric statement, not a simultaneous extremizer claim
for several cap directions.

First verify uniqueness in(11). Put a=beta-1>0. A direct derivative is

    [u^d/(a+u)]''
      =u^(d-2)[d(d-1)a^2+2d(d-2)au+(d-1)(d-2)u^2]/(a+u)^3>0

for0<u<1 and d>=2. Thus g''>0. The right side of(11) has derivative
(1-u)g''(u)>0 on(0,1), value0 at u=0, and value g(1)=1 at u=1.
This proves its claimed range and uniqueness.

For lambda>sigma beta set u=1-sigma beta/lambda. Formula(9) becomes

    vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T))=V g(u).

Indeed (lambda-1)/(lambda-sigma)
=[sigma beta-1+u]/[sigma(beta-1+u)], which gives exactly(10).
Put

    Phi(lambda)=integral(lambda-r_e)_+ ell dnu
               =lambda Vg(u).

Its left and right derivatives are respectively the ell-weighted
measures of {r_e<lambda} and {r_e<=lambda}. The difference quotients
are bounded by ell, whose integral is V. The explicit formula for Phi
is differentiable, so both derivatives agree and the equality level
has zero ell-weighted measure. Differentiation yields

    Phi'(lambda)=V[g(u)+(1-u)g'(u)],
    lambda Phi'(lambda)-Phi(lambda)=V sigma beta g'(u). (13)

Apply(3)--(4) at the lambda corresponding to(11). They give the lower
bound(12) for every actual B of volume b.

It remains to show attainment by a convex subbody; a relaxed column
optimization alone would not suffice. Let

    E_lambda=pi_e[T intersect F_lambda(T)],
    B_lambda=T intersect pi_e^(-1)(E_lambda).

The overlap is a full-dimensional simplex for lambda>sigma beta, so
its projection E_lambda is a full-dimensional convex compact set in
the transverse space. Hence B_lambda is a convex body. Up to null
boundary sections, E_lambda is exactly the set of T columns with
r_e<=lambda, by the overlap length identity. Thus B_lambda takes
the whole T section on precisely these columns. Equation(13) gives
its volume as Phi'(lambda)=b. Its roof integral is

    integral_{r_e<=lambda} r_e ell dnu
       =lambda Phi'(lambda)-Phi(lambda),

the expression in(12). This proves actual convex attainment for0<b<V.

When b=V, take B=T and u=1. The integrals

    lambda[V-vol_d(T intersect F_lambda(T))]
       =integral min{lambda ell,h+U}dnu

increase to R_e(T,h). Formula(9), or its finite binomial expansion,
therefore gives

    R_e(T,h)=V[d sigma beta-(sigma-1)]
            =V sigma beta g'(1),

agreeing with(12). This handles the endpoint without assuming a finite
optimizing lambda.

For sigma=1, g(u)=u^d, so u=eta from(1) and(12) reduces to the
universal sharp value in(2). For sigma>1 it quantifies the additional
cost of that actual direction and retains its actual convex optimizer.

# A sharp simplex roof bound in every dimension and direction

**Sharp simplex roof integral in every direction**

Let d>=2, and let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole dependence sum_i v_i=0, so T={x:v_i.x<=1 for all i} is a bounded simplex of volume V. For e with v_0.e=1 use t=v_0.x, x=y+t e, y in ker(v_0), and transverse measure dnu=dH_(d-1)/||v_0||. Let B subset T be a convex d-body of volume 0<b<=V with upper t-section endpoint U_B(y). If h>d, H=h+1, and eta is the UNIQUE number in (0,1] satisfying b/V=d eta^(d-1)-(d-1)eta^d, then integral_(pi_e B)(h+U_B)dnu >= H V d/(d+1) eta^(d-1). This is sharp, over the allowed bodies and directions, for every b; it is strict when some v_i.e>0 with i!=0.

Scope limits: A continuous subbody/roof theorem, not an OC center theorem. Partial columns and physical Jacobians are essential.
